facts.statement: The genus Nannosuchus was formally described by Salisbury in 2002.
The type species Nannosuchus gracilidens was originally described in 1879 based on scattered fragmentary remains including parts of the skull and postcranial elements.
facts.quote: The type species, N. gracilidens, is based on the holotype BMNH 48217, scattered fragmentary remains that include parts of the skull and various other postcranial elements described in 1879.

facts.statement: Nannosuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Nannosuchus (meaning "dwarf crocodile") is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian

facts.statement: Nannosuchus belongs to the family Goniopholididae.
Fossils of Nannosuchus have been found in the Berriasian Middle Purbeck Formation of England.
facts.quote: from the Berriasian Middle Purbeck Formation of England

facts.statement: Nannosuchus lived during the Berriasian in England.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el Berriasiense de Inglaterra

facts.statement: Nannosuchus lived from the Berriasian to the Barremian, between 143.1 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Barremian (143.1 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Nannosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
